newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil stocks end softer after day of record trade.
newsitem.headline: Brazil stocks end softer after day of record trade.

text.p: Brazil stocks ended down Thursday on profit-taking, slipping late in the session on blue-chip sales on a day of record-high trading volume, brokers said.
The Sao Paulo bourse's Bovespa index of 48 most-traded shares closed off 1.37 percent at 12,874 points in whopping trade totalling 1.757 billion reais ($1.634 billion).
"That's an historical record on a day without options," one broker said. The bolsa confirmed it was a record.

Brokers said Brazilian investment funds poured money into local shares early in the day, continuing a trend that has fueled a bull market for the last several weeks and driving prices and volume skyward.
But the flow of cash tapered off late in the session and blue chip shares were hit by some profit-taking as investors began to round out portfolios ahead of the end of the first semester.
Still, dealers said it is too early to say if there is a shift in trading patterns.
"It's too early to say," one dealer said. "There's still a lot of money coming in. People are still enthusiastic and there's no news that could cause the market to drop."
He added that most of the day's volume was registered early in the session, when shares were up strongly over Wednesday's close and prices fell at session's end when trade was light.
Benchmark blue chip Telebras preferred declined 0.71 percent to end at 167.50 reais but other blue chips, especially those that surged in recent sessions, fell further.
State oil firm Petrobras slipped 2.82 percent top close at 310 reais while federal power holding Eletrobras dropped 4.49 percent to close at 660 reais.
Sao Paulo state's Cesp plunged 5.44 percent to end at 72.80 reais, leading the drop in power shares which had soared in recent weeks on bright prospects for the sector's privatization.
The bolsa's Electrical Energy Index .IEE slipped 2.43 percent to end at 3,425 points.
